function.name: search_notes
function.description: Search notes by content, tags, and/or date range. All parameters are optional but at least one should be provided. Use tags to filter by category (e.g. tags=["meeting"] for meeting notes, tags=["project"] for project notes). Multiple tags use AND logic — only notes matching all tags are returned. Use date_from/date_to for time-based queries; a single day query should use the same date for both. Combine parameters to narrow results (e.g. tags + date range together). Returns up to 10 matching notes with path, title, tags, and dates.

query.description: Full-text search query. Use for topic or content-based searches. Do NOT use this for category names like 'meeting notes' or 'research notes' — use tags instead.

tags.description: Filter by tags using AND logic. Tag values are lowercase strings like 'meeting', 'project', 'journal', 'reference', 'deep-learning', 'nlp', 'python', 'attention', 'transformer'.

date_from.description: Start of date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). Based on note creation date.

date_to.description: End of date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (inclusive). For a single-day query, set date_from and date_to to the same value.

function.name: get_note
function.description: Retrieve the full content of a specific note by its exact title or file path. Use this when the user names a specific note. Title is the filename without extension and with underscores replaced by spaces (e.g. 'Self Attention' for Self_Attention.md). If the note is not found, use search_notes to discover the correct title first.

path.description: File path of the note, e.g. 'research/Transformers.md'. Use this if you already know the exact path.

title.description: Title of the note — the filename without .md extension, with underscores replaced by spaces. Example: 'CNN Architecture', 'Python Tips', 'Reinforcement Learning'.

function.name: get_related_notes
function.description: Find notes connected to a specific note through wiki-style [[links]]. Use this for queries about references, backlinks, or graph connections — e.g. 'what notes link to X?', 'what does X reference?', 'what is connected to X?'. Direction 'incoming' finds notes that link TO the given note (backlinks). Direction 'outgoing' finds notes that the given note links TO (its references/prerequisites). Direction 'both' returns all connected notes. Title must be the exact note title (filename without .md, underscores as spaces). Returns up to 10 results per direction.

path.description: File path of the note, e.g. 'research/Transformers.md'.

title.description: Title of the note (filename without .md, underscores replaced by spaces). Example: 'Transformers', 'Attention Mechanisms', 'Paper Recommender'.

direction.description: Which links to return. 'incoming' = notes that link TO this note. 'outgoing' = notes this note links TO. 'both' = all connected notes.

function.name: get_vault_overview
function.description: Get vault statistics (total notes, folder breakdown, tag counts) and the 5 most recently modified notes. Use this to orient when the user asks about the vault structure or recent activity.

function.name: create_note
function.description: Create a new markdown note in the vault. Use when the user asks to write, create, or synthesize a new note. The note is immediately searchable after creation. You may first retrieve existing notes with get_note or search_notes to gather content before writing the new note.

title.description: Title of the new note. Use Title Case with spaces (e.g. 'Attention Survey', 'Project Status'). Do not include .md extension.

folder.description: Destination folder. Must be one of: research, projects, meetings, daily, reference.

content.description: Markdown body of the note. May include headings, lists, and wiki-style [[links]] to other notes.

tags.description: List of lowercase tags, e.g. ['research', 'deep-learning'] or ['meeting', 'advisor'].
